raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview Python's `GET /server_info` (dev mode) returns the API server's `VllmConfig`, synced from every engine's ready response. The Rust frontend returns its own frontend `Config` under the same key, which has no `model_config`, `cache_config` or `parallel_config`, so the DP `server_info` tests (`v1/distributed/test_{internal,external,hybrid}_lb_dp.py -k server_info`) fail under Rust with `KeyError: 'parallel_config'`. This PR has each engine send its `VllmConfig` dump in the ready response (dev mode only), and the Rust `/server_info` reports it with the API-server view applied. ## Claims - Under the Rust frontend, `/server_info` returns `vllm_config` in the shape Python returns, with the fields Python's API server derives from its engines (`data_parallel_size`, summed `num_gpu_blocks`, minimum `max_model_len`, common `effective_attention_block_size`, `_api_process_count`/`_api_process_rank`). - The Rust frontend's own config moves to a separate `rust_frontend_config` key. - Outside `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, engines do no extra work: the ready-response field stays `None`. ## Validation Commands from `.buildkite/scripts/run-rust-frontend-cargo-ci.sh` (`style-clippy` and `test`), run from the repo root: ``` cargo fmt --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --all -- --check # ok cargo sort --workspace --check rust # ok cargo deny --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --config rust/deny.toml check bans # ok cargo clippy --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings # ok cargo nextest run --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml --workspace --all-features --locked --no-fail-fast # 2311 tests run: 2311 passed, 13 skipped ``` - `server_info::tests::engine_vllm_config_reports_frontend_view`: two dense DP engines (ranks 4 and 5 of DP=8) report DP=1, 10 and 20 blocks, `max_model_len` 8192 and 4096, and attention block sizes 64 and 128; `/server_info` reports DP=8, rank 4, 30 blocks, 4096, a `null` attention block size and `_api_process_*` 1/0. It fails with the overlay removed. - `python_msgpack_fixtures_match_rust_encoding` decodes a Python-encoded `vllm_config`. - `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and the pre-commit mypy wrapper pass on the changed Python files. - GPU, one 4-GPU node, `TP_SIZE=1`, model `ibm-research/PowerMoE-3b`, on an earlier `main`. Before this change, every `server_info` case failed under Rust with `KeyError: 'parallel_config'`: ``` # Rust frontend, whole files: DP_SIZE=4 v1/distributed/test_internal_lb_dp.py # 9 passed, 1 failed: server_info[4] DP_SIZE=2 v1/distributed/test_external_lb_dp.py # 15 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed: server_info[api-4-standard] DP_SIZE=4 v1/distributed/test_hybrid_lb_dp.py # 5 passed, 1 failed: server_info[4] # Python frontend, -k server_info (the engine now sends the dump in dev mode): internal 2 passed; external 3 passed; hybrid 2 passed ``` The remaining Rust failures are the `api_server_count=4` cases: the Rust frontend runs one API process by design. ## Details Rust has no `VllmConfig` of its own. A Python launcher could pass one at startup, but `vllm-rs serve` launches the Python engine itself, and remote headless engines have no launcher on the frontend's node. Every engine already sends `EngineCoreReadyResponse` for post-initialization config (`max_model_len` after auto-fit, `num_gpu_blocks` after profiling), so the config travels there. - Python engine (`vllm/v1/engine/__init__.py`, `core.py`): `EngineCoreReadyResponse` gets a trailing `vllm_config: dict[str, Any] | None = None`. `_make_ready_response` fills it with the same JSON-mode dump Python's `/server_info` uses, only when `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE` is set. The struct is a msgpack map, so an older peer on either side ignores or defaults the key. The Python client ignores it. - Rust protocol (`engine-core-client`): the matching `#[serde(default)] vllm_config: Option`; the Python fixture and the key-drift test cover it. - Rust `/server_info` (`server/src/server_info.rs`): `ServerInfoSnapshot::from_engine` takes the first engine's dump and replaces the fields Python reports from the API server's view, because each engine reports its own values: | Field | Value | Source | |---|---|---| | `parallel_config._api_process_count`, `_api_process_rank` | 1, 0 | the Rust frontend is the only API process | | `parallel_config.data_parallel_size`, `data_parallel_rank` | deployment size, first engine's rank | same as the gRPC `GetServerInfo` parallelism view | | `cache_config.num_gpu_blocks` | sum over engines | `total_num_gpu_blocks()`, as Python sums | | `cache_config.effective_attention_block_size` | the common value, or `null` if engines differ | as Python | | `model_config.max_model_len` | minimum over engines | `max_model_len()`, as Python | An engine that sends no dump (a remote headless engine started without `VLLM_SERVER_DEV_MODE`, or an older engine) gives `vllm_config: null`. Engines started by `vllm serve` or `vllm-rs serve` inherit the frontend's environment, so in dev mode they always send it. - The Rust frontend `Config`, which shares none of `VllmConfig`'s structure, is reported as `rust_frontend_config`. `config_format=text` renders both with the existing Rust renderer, not Python's `str(VllmConfig)`. The engine owns the config and only serializes it; the frontend view belongs to the Rust server's `/server_info` snapshot, next to the gRPC server-info view it mirrors. Remaining differences, unchanged here: - `--api-server-count N` cases expect N API processes; the Rust frontend runs one. - Per-engine fields that Python's API server does not sync (for example `data_parallel_rank_local`, `data_parallel_index`) show the first engine's values. So does `data_parallel_size_local`: the frontend knows how many engines it connects to, not how many run on its node. - `system_env` stays the Rust subset (`arch`, `family`, `os`). Not a duplicate: no open PR changes `/server_info` on the Rust frontend. AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to prepare this change; the human submitter reviewed every changed line. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01K2SEJPm2Mawmm6pu8m9E1o ---

(Mandatory for agents, optional for humans). - [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR. - [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. - [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI. - [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples. - [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
